question.text: In case of a Category III AIF with a breach of its permitted leverage limits, by when must the custodian report the breach to SEBI?

answer.text: Within the same working day of breach
Before 10:00 AM on the next working day
Within 30 days of breach through the merchant banker

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per Section 13.7.2, in case of a Category III AIF with a breach of its permitted leverage limits, the custodian shall report to SEBI providing name of the fund, extent of breach, and reasons for the same BEFORE 10:00 AM on the next working day. **The Trap:** Same-day is too aggressive; 7 days / 30 days too lax for a leverage breach. The 10 AM next-working-day cut-off is highly specific. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-B (Cat III distributor) lightly covers this. XIX-C manager-side requires knowing the exact reporting timeline to coordinate with custodian SLAs. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Automate pre-trade leverage limit checks at the OMS (order management system) level — relying only on custodian post-trade monitoring means breaches cost you T+1 SEBI reporting and reputational damage.
